column20: What went wrong and why? - caused by a degradation in the redo process on one of the secondary copies servicing the US geography
column21: What went wrong and why? - AVD relies on SQL Database to store configuration data; degradation in the US geo database caused failures to access service resources
column22: What happened? - configuration and metadata stored in the US Geography which we host in the East US 2 region; impact across nine US regions
column23: What happened? - This event impacted customers in the following US regions: Central US, East US, East US 2, North Central US, South Central US, West Central US, West US, West US 2, and West US 3
column24: How did we respond? 19:02 UTC - the friendly geo failover operation failed since it could not synchronize data between the geo secondary and the unavailable geo primary; end users with connections established via any of these US regions may also have been impacted
column25: How did we respond? 18:57 UTC - automation attempted a friendly geo failover; 19:02 UTC it failed; 19:59 UTC manual forced geo-failover started; 20:00 UTC completed; 20:36 UTC customer impact mitigated
column26: no statement of a central controller or orchestrator; impact traced to the redo process on the SQL secondary copy
column27: V8b no - end users with connections established via any of these US regions may also have been impacted; V8a and V8c - no statement found
column28: V1 coded other because the report names an SQL redo-pipeline defect and no release or config change; V3 coded shared_global because the US-geography database served nine US regions
